key_insight: A GPU-accelerated one-way Eulerian-Lagrangian framework can efficiently simulate 2D incompressible fluid flow and particle transport while capturing key turbulent dispersion and inertia effects.
engineering_relevance: The method provides a practical, modular solver for studying particle-laden turbulence with good accuracy, statistical robustness, and single-GPU efficiency.
method: 2D incompressible Navier–Stokes solved with a Fourier pseudospectral Eulerian fluid solver and second-order Adams–Bashforth time stepping
Passive tracer and finite-inertia particle trajectories advanced with classical fourth-order Runge–Kutta
Fluid-to-particle coupling via bilinear, bicubic Catmull-Rom, or bicubic B-spline interpolation
evidence_signal: The framework was verified against analytical solutions and benchmark problems, and showed particle-number convergence plus similar transport statistics for bilinear and higher-order interpolation.
watch_item: The coupling is one-way and relies on interpolation accuracy, so it may be less suitable for strongly two-way coupled particle-fluid systems or flows where subgrid particle forcing matters.
paper_title: A coupled Eulerian Lagrangian approach for fluid and particle dynamics
